# Introduction

I checked the factor structure and reliability of R3 (Q3–Q6) and R6 (Q31–Q34) to see whether the items can be combined into composite scales.

# Data Preparation

```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)

data <- read_sav("Case31_NS_cleaned.sav")

employee_items <- data |>
  select(q3:q6) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), \(x) !is.na(x)))

operations_items <- data |>
  select(q31:q34) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), \(x) !is.na(x)))

combined_items <- data |>
  select(q3:q6, q31:q34) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |>
  filter(if_all(everything(), \(x) !is.na(x)))
```

I used complete responses for each analysis. R6 only includes Q31–Q34, as specified in the instructions.

```{r}
#| include: false

fmt <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)

factor_table <- function(model) {data.frame(Item = rownames(model$loadings),
                                            as.matrix(model$loadings),
                                            Communality = model$communality,
                                            row.names = NULL)}
```

# R3: Employee Proficiency

## Factor Analysis

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

employee_parallel <- fa.parallel(employee_items,
                                 fa = "fa",
                                 fm = "minres",
                                 n.iter = 100,
                                 plot = FALSE)

employee_fa <- fa(employee_items,
                  nfactors = 1,
                  rotate = "none",
                  fm = "minres")

factor_table(employee_fa) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Parallel analysis suggests **`r employee_parallel$nfact` factor(s)**. The absolute loadings range from **`r fmt(min(abs(employee_fa$loadings)))` to `r fmt(max(abs(employee_fa$loadings)))`**. Communalities show how much of each item's variance the factor explains.

`r if (employee_parallel$nfact == 1 && all(abs(employee_fa$loadings) >= .40) && all(employee_fa$communality >= .30)) "The items fit one factor reasonably well, supporting convergent validity." else "The results do not clearly support treating all four items as one factor, so convergent validity is questionable."`

## Reliability

```{r}
employee_alpha <- psych::alpha(employee_items,
                               check.keys = FALSE)

employee_alpha$total |>
  select(raw_alpha, std.alpha, average_r) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Cronbach's alpha is **`r fmt(employee_alpha$total$raw_alpha)`**. `r if (employee_alpha$total$raw_alpha >= .70) "This meets the .70 guideline for acceptable internal consistency." else "This falls below the .70 guideline for acceptable internal consistency."`

# R6: Operational Effectiveness

## Factor Analysis

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

operations_parallel <- fa.parallel(operations_items,
                                   fa = "fa",
                                   fm = "minres",
                                   n.iter = 100,
                                   plot = FALSE)

operations_fa <- fa(operations_items,
                    nfactors = 1,
                    rotate = "none",
                    fm = "minres")

factor_table(operations_fa) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Parallel analysis suggests **`r operations_parallel$nfact` factor(s)**. The absolute loadings range from **`r fmt(min(abs(operations_fa$loadings)))` to `r fmt(max(abs(operations_fa$loadings)))`**.

`r if (operations_parallel$nfact == 1 && all(abs(operations_fa$loadings) >= .40) && all(operations_fa$communality >= .30)) "The items fit one factor reasonably well, supporting convergent validity." else "The results do not clearly support one operational-effectiveness factor. Weaker loadings or communalities indicate that some items do not fit the scale well."`

## Reliability

```{r}
operations_alpha <- psych::alpha(operations_items,
                                 check.keys = FALSE)

operations_alpha$total |>
  select(raw_alpha, std.alpha, average_r) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Cronbach's alpha is **`r fmt(operations_alpha$total$raw_alpha)`**. `r if (operations_alpha$total$raw_alpha >= .70) "This meets the .70 guideline for acceptable internal consistency." else "This falls below .70, so the items do not have acceptable internal consistency."`

# Discriminant Validity

I analyzed all eight items together to check whether the two scales separate as expected. I used oblimin rotation because the factors could be related.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

combined_parallel <- fa.parallel(combined_items,
                                 fa = "fa",
                                 fm = "minres",
                                 n.iter = 100,
                                 plot = FALSE)

combined_fa <- fa(combined_items,
                  nfactors = 2,
                  rotate = "oblimin",
                  fm = "minres")

factor_table(combined_fa) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

combined_fa$Phi |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Factor correlation")
```

```{r}
#| include: false

loadings <- abs(as.matrix(combined_fa$loadings))
primary_factor <- max.col(loadings, ties.method = "first")

distinct_scales <-
  combined_parallel$nfact == 2 &&
  length(unique(primary_factor[1:4])) == 1 &&
  length(unique(primary_factor[5:8])) == 1 &&
  primary_factor[1] != primary_factor[5] &&
  all(apply(loadings, 1, max) >= .40) &&
  all(apply(loadings, 1, min) < .30) &&
  abs(combined_fa$Phi[1, 2]) < .85
```

Parallel analysis suggests **`r combined_parallel$nfact` factor(s)**. `r if (distinct_scales) "Q3–Q6 and Q31–Q34 separate into their expected factors, with limited cross-loadings. This supports discriminant validity." else "The results do not clearly separate the items into the two expected scales. Discriminant validity is not well supported."` Extracting two factors by itself does not confirm that the scales are distinct.

# Decision about Composite Scales

```{r}
#| include: false

employee_composite <-
  employee_parallel$nfact == 1 &&
  all(abs(employee_fa$loadings) >= .40) &&
  all(employee_fa$communality >= .30) &&
  employee_alpha$total$raw_alpha >= .70

operations_composite <-
  operations_parallel$nfact == 1 &&
  all(abs(operations_fa$loadings) >= .40) &&
  all(operations_fa$communality >= .30) &&
  operations_alpha$total$raw_alpha >= .70
```

**R3:** `r if (employee_composite) "I would average Q3–Q6 into an employee-proficiency composite based on the factor and reliability results." else "I would keep Q3–Q6 separate because the factor and reliability results do not consistently support one composite."`

**R6:** `r if (operations_composite) "I would average Q31–Q34 into an operational-effectiveness composite based on the factor and reliability results." else "I would keep Q31–Q34 separate because the factor and reliability results do not consistently support one composite."`

`r if (!distinct_scales) "The lack of clear discriminant validity also means I would be cautious about interpreting these as separate constructs." else "The combined analysis supports treating the two constructs separately."`
